day01: Day one of making my dream game.
It's called, The Bear Must Eat.
Office bears get off work at five p.m., and raid your pond for fish.
You're the fox who owns the pond.
This brown square? That's a bear. Trust me.
First test. Walk to the pond.
Tomorrow, fish. What fish should I add?
day02: Every fish just wanders around the pond, doing fish stuff.
If two happy fish bump into each other... baby fish.
Then I changed one line of code, and every fish did this.
They all went to the corner. All of them. Why?
I forgot to normalize one vector.
Fixed. Now they spread out, and the pond fills up on its own.
day03: and every single bear runs to my pond.
They cannonball in, grab a fish, and pay me five coins each.
This is the whole game, and I love it.
They're just standing in the water. Confused.
day04: Day four. Time to replace the orange square.
That square is Reynard. The fox who owns the pond.
I built him out of tiny cubes, one layer at a time.
Then I gave him way too many animations.
day05: This is the office bear. He can walk, eat, and roar.
Then I made a few more. Grandma, construction, and the CEO.
Now the brown squares get promoted.
They cannonball in, they swim, they eat.
The world is still squares though. Tomorrow.
day06: Day six. The world is still squares.
So I drew the whole thing.
Grass, trees, flowers, rocks, lily pads, and real fish.
Then I added a day and night cycle.
Same pond as day one, by the way.
day07: Day seven. Adding your comments to my game.
Add a banana fish. Say less.
I drew it pixel by pixel. Brown spots, little stem for a tail.
Then I put it in the game.
It's a banana. It's a fish. It's beautiful.
And yes, the bears eat it.
day08: You can build a little restaurant around the pond now.
Every piece goes plonk, with a dust puff and a pow.
Tables, a barbecue, a jukebox, and a neon sign.
And at five p.m., they actually use it.
day09: Day nine. The game worked, but it felt dead.
Comic words. Squash and stretch. Screen shake. Coins. And way too many sound effects.
day10: Day ten. I made a title screen.
There's always a bear in the pond. Always.
Ten days ago, this was a brown square walking on water.
There's still so much to do. Should I keep going?
